title: Tencent's First Dedicated AI Gaming Companion, Goose Dimension, Enters Closed Beta: Letting AI Dive Into the Game Screen to Team Up With You

content_html:
Do you always feel like you're missing a teammate when gaming alone? Tencent has tucked the solution right into your screen. On November 10, Tencent's first dedicated AI game companion Agent, "Eciyuan", quietly entered beta testing. As a company with a vast portfolio of game IP, Tencent has moved AI beyond customer service and tools and placed it right beside players' screens. The product targets PC players, offering human-like companionship and real-time voice interaction, aiming to fill the experience gap of "having someone to play with" outside competitive play.

AI can "see" what you're playing

Eciyuan's selling point is real-time companionship rather than blind chatting: it can read the player's game screen and then talk with them based on what is actually happening on screen. If you're stuck, or don't understand a piece of equipment or a mechanic, just ask at any time, and the AI will answer based on the current screen. It's like having an extra knowledgeable friend sitting next to your monitor—always on call and able to understand the state of the match.

It can also chat with you on QQ and change voices

In addition to following you through games, Eciyuan also connects companion chat between PC and mobile QQ, so players can keep chatting after leaving their computer. The product also offers desktop pets, one-click wallpaper changes, and fun features such as "speaking on your behalf" and "voice changing", though the latter few will arrive in later versions. The virtual characters currently listed on the official website are Xiaxia, Shen Lubai, Guyu, and Bella. All of them are familiar with popular competitive games such as Valorant, League of Legends, and Counter-Strike, and can keep up with all kinds of topics players bring up in those games.

Game companionship is becoming a new battleground for big tech companies. As Tencent brings AI to players' side, whether it can sustain the long-term stickiness of an "electronic companion" will still depend on beta feedback and future polishing of its features.
